subject: Capacity sizing: 65k-context model + quantization impact for reserved pool
messages:
From: Cara Lin <cara.lin@bioquant.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: salesops@bioquant.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing for 65k-context model + quantization question

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — we want to move from a POC to a Reserved (Dedicated) pool for a new product feature that requires a 65k token context window. High-level ask: we plan to serve a custom Llama-derivative model (parameter count ~36B) with aggressive 4-bit quantization as an option to save capacity. Target workload: peak of ~18 requests/sec with median request size ~4k tokens (many long-context retrievals up to full 65k). Latency SLO is 350ms p50 for interactive flows, and we have a batch path for async scoring.

Questions:
- Can you outline recommended GPU types and counts for reserved capacity under (A) baseline FP16, (B) 8-bit quant, (C) 4-bit quant?
- How should we size KV cache per active session (estimated active sessions 1.2k) and how does that affect replica sizing?
- Any gotchas for fallback (hosted -> dedicated) if we need to degrade context length under heavy load?

I've attached a CSV with our token distribution and a short profile. Procurement target: contract signed by end of August. Happy to set up a call.

Thanks,
Cara
Cara Lin
Head of Platform Eng
BioQuant Therapeutics

Attachments: bioquant-context-profile.csv

Hi Cara — thanks for the details and the profile. Quick confirmation items before Marcus and I put together a formal sizing:

1) Is the 65k context requirement a hard SLO (must support full KV for all interactive requests), or can you tolerate a step-down to 32k for a small percentage (e.g., 10%) of requests during peak?
2) Do you need encryption-managed keys (HSM) in the Private control plane or is hosted key management sufficient? Procurement/enterprise buyers ask about that early.
3) Do you expect many concurrent long streams (i.e., many requests that iterate and extend KV across multiple messages) or are long contexts mainly from single-shot retrieval-augmented prompts?

If you can answer those, Marcus will size GPUs and KV cache calculations; we can include cost delta between quant levels and a conservative reserved pool layout to meet your p50 SLO. I penciled August 2nd for an internal deck and will share a spreadsheet.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for 65k-context model + quantization question

Hi Cara / team — I ran the numbers from the token distribution you sent and sketched three conservative reserved pool options. Key assumptions: model ~36B parameters; KV cache stores past key/value for the attention mechanism at float16-equivalent size before quantized runtime packing; 65k context implies ~65k * per-token KV footprint. We assume 80GB-class GPUs (A100/H100 equivalently sized) for headroom with pipelines pinned to single-GPU replicas in the initial rollout.

Option A — FP16 baseline (no runtime quantization):
- KV memory per active session: ~65k tokens * 2 vectors/token * 2 bytes/q (after packing) ~= 520 MB/session (conservative 600MB/session with overhead).
- Active sessions estimate 1.2k => KV aggregate ~720 GB.
- Model GPU memory (weights + activation buffers) per replica: ~60 GB usable for model + runtime.
- Recommended fleet: 12 x 80GB GPUs (A100/H100) in reserved pool. This yields ~1.2k sessions distributed with KV either in host persistent RAM + fast NVMe spill or sharded across nodes; we recommend per-GPU local NVMe cache and a KV eviction policy to keep interactive p50.

Option B — 8-bit quant (INT8/8-bit TF32-like kernels):
- Model memory drops ~30% -> usable model memory requirement ~42 GB.
- KV cache unchanged (KV remains high-precision for attention; we do not reduce KV to 8-bit by default because of quality regressions on long context).
- Recommended fleet: 9 x 80GB GPUs.
- Notes: unit-cost drop ~20-28% vs FP16 once inference kernels are warmed; profiling needed for throughput saturation points because quant kernels increase compute intensity per token differently.

Option C — aggressive 4-bit quant (product-quality tuned):
- Model memory drops ~55-60% -> ~25 GB model footprint, freeing memory for larger KV residency.
- If you accept an engineered 4-bit KV compression scheme (lossy quant for cached KV) we can drop per-session KV from ~600MB -> ~180MB (about 3x reduction) but expect possible tail-quality regressions on tasks that rely on precise token alignments at 65k.
- Recommended fleet (with KV compression): 6 x 80GB GPUs (conservative).
- Trade-offs: lower unit GPU count and cost, but increased engineering risk, and slower time-to-first-byte until kernels are optimized for 4-bit KV access patterns. Also increases operator complexity for rollouts and fallback.

Throughput/latency sizing notes: to meet p50 350ms interactive SLO at 18 rps peak and average 4k request token length, we need headroom for burst ~30 rps. The 12-GPU FP16 layout gives ~25-30% spare capacity for rolling maintenance; the 6-GPU 4-bit layout is tighter on headroom and requires aggressive batching/caching.

Fallback and rollout suggestions:
- Canary with model variants: publish a 65k-capable FP16 variant and a 65k-capable 4-bit variant; route traffic by policy (tenancy or percentage) and monitor quality delta on eval prompt set.
- Graceful step-down: allow runtime truncation from 65k->32k for lowest-priority requests via routing policy; do not silently evict KV from active interactive sessions.
- KV tiering: keep hot KV in GPU-local memory for top 200 sessions; spill cold KV to NVMe with a prefetcher for session reactivation.

Attached is a quick workbook with per-GPU math and cost deltas (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) and a short PDF describing KV memory profiling heuristics (kvcache-memory-profile.pdf). Happy to walk through the numbers in a 30-minute architecture call.

—Marcus Lin
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, kvcache-memory-profile.pdf
